The Division also elected to partially remove the 203(b)(8) exemption with respect to New Jersey cities within 5 miles of New York City and municipalities in Westchester and Nassau Counties, so that the city of New York would not be included in the commercial zones of these suburban municipalities.
At the interim stage of this proceeding, we were persuaded by the economic data submitted by New York area shippers that the extent of commercial zone activity in and around New York City should be described by reference to the revised population-mileage formula. Shippers states that the confusing nature of existing New York City commercial zone rules inhibit the free flow of local commerce, and the restrictive zone limits hamper business in the search for suitable locations. Specifically, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey and certain other shippers submitted maps and statistical information demonstrating the dispersal from 1939 to 1972 of manufacturing and wholesale trade establishments and the present disbribution pattern of business location.
